page: The Microsoft Azure E2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core using two threads per core. Hardware instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache.

System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is bundled with an 81 GB local SSD and supports premium storage configurations, with no physical GPU provisioned. Benchmark evaluations show balanced single-core execution, achieving 1887.88 in stress-ng and 1626.0 in Geekbench single-core tests. Due to its two-vCPU footprint, parallel compute capacity remains limited, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 1932.27 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 1899.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth registers at 14.47 GB/sec, while write operations reach 13.5 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the E2ds_v5 is its low aggregate multi-core throughput in exchange for substantial memory per core. Application-level metrics reflect this distribution, delivering 1.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.71 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. From an operational cost-efficiency perspective, the instance prevents over-provisioning compute cores simply to satisfy memory requirements. The configuration is directly aligned with memory-bound workloads that do not demand extensive parallel thread scaling, including distributed cache nodes, lightweight relational database servers, and memory-heavy application middleware.
description: The Microsoft Azure E2ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of RAM, and an 81 GB local SSD with no bundled GPUs. The instance exhibits an 8.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio, delivering average single-thread performance alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to its low core count. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates capable single-core execution with 1887.88 in stress-ng and 1626.0 in Geekbench, while achieving 1.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.71 GB/sec in static web serving. Offering high memory density relative to compute allocation, the E2ds_v5 provides a cost-effective footprint for memory-dependent applications that do not demand extensive multi-core parallelism, such as small caching tiers, lightweight databases, and memory-intensive staging environments.
